# Golden fixture pack

Test inputs for SBAM (issue E0.8). **Every file here is synthetic**: a fictional company (Alpha Dynamics Ltd,
Rocketreach in the masters sample), example.com addresses, no real client data, no phone numbers, no secrets.

## Using the fixtures

```python
from fixtures import blob, copy_to_tmp, eicar_bytes, fixture_path

path = fixture_path("documents", "text.pdf")                      # read-only input
editable = copy_to_tmp("documents", "sample.csv", tmp_path=tmp_path)  # copy before changing anything
eicar = eicar_bytes()                                             # built at runtime, never committed
too_big = blob(15 * 1024 * 1024 + 1)                              # exact size, never committed
```

- Fixtures are **read-only**. A test that mutates one copies it with `copy_to_tmp` first.
- The plain EICAR string is never in Git (it would trip antivirus on laptops and on GitHub). `malware/eicar.b64`
  holds it encoded and `eicar_bytes()` decodes it (68 bytes).
- Large files are generated by `blob(n)`; nothing over a few hundred KB is stored.
- `SHA256SUMS` records every fixture file (not this README or the helper code). Verify with `cd server/tests/fixtures && sha256sum -c SHA256SUMS`.
- `python server/tests/fixtures/check_fixture_readme.py` fails if a file is not listed in this README.
- Regenerate the documents deliberately with `uv run scripts/generate_test_fixtures.py`, then commit them together
  with the new `SHA256SUMS`. `sow/sow_rfq_nav9.json` and this README are written by hand.

## documents/

Client-document samples, one per MVP file type (TD §5.2). They tell one story: an RFQ for the NAV-9 board.

| File | What it is | Expected outcome |
|---|---|---|
| `documents/text.pdf` | Text-based PDF, 2 pages | Text extracted with page provenance; OCR not used |
| `documents/scanned_full.pdf` | Scanned PDF: 2 image-only pages | Detected as scanned; each page goes to OCR |
| `documents/scanned_mixed.pdf` | Page 1 has a text layer, page 2 is image-only | Page 1 read as text, page 2 sent to OCR (mixed case) |
| `documents/fake_pdf_is_png.pdf` | A PNG saved with a `.pdf` name | Type detection by magic bytes reports an image, not a PDF |
| `documents/sample.docx` | Word document: heading, paragraphs, a 3-column table | Text and table extracted |
| `documents/multi_sheet.xlsx` | Workbook with sheets `BOM`, `Suppliers`, `Notes` and merged cells | Sheet and cell provenance kept; merged cells handled |
| `documents/sample.csv` | BOM lines as CSV | Rows parsed with line provenance |
| `documents/sample.md` | Markdown with headings and lists | Headings and structure preserved |
| `documents/sample.txt` | Plain text | Ingested as text |
| `documents/with_attachment.eml` | Email whose attachment is `rfq_scan.pdf` (identical to `documents/scanned_full.pdf`) | Headers and body parsed; the attachment becomes a child document, scanned and sent to OCR |
| `documents/sample.json` | A rule as JSON | Structural pre-parse, key paths kept |
| `documents/sample.yaml` | A rule as YAML | Structural pre-parse, key paths kept |
| `documents/sample.xml` | BOM as XML | Structural pre-parse, key paths kept |
| `documents/openapi.yaml` | Small OpenAPI 3.0.3 description | Recognized as an API spec and pre-parsed |
| `documents/fastmcp_spec.json` | Small FastMCP tool specification | Recognized as a FastMCP spec and pre-parsed |
| `documents/sample.py` | Python source with a function and a class | Symbols extracted with Python `ast` |
| `documents/sample.sql` | SQL: one table, one query | Ingested as source text |
| `documents/sample.js` | JavaScript source | Ingested as plain text (basic) |
| `documents/sample.go` | Go source | Ingested as plain text (basic) |
| `documents/sample.cpp` | C++ source | Ingested as plain text (basic) |
| `documents/scan.png` | The scanned RFQ page as a PNG (827x1169, grayscale) | OCR returns the page text |
| `documents/photo.jpg` | The same page as a JPEG | OCR returns the page text |
| `documents/scan.tiff` | The same page as a TIFF | OCR returns the page text |
| `documents/sample.zip` | Zip with `rfq_summary.md` and `bom_extract.csv` | Each member ingested as its own document; members count toward the 20-file limit |
| `documents/sample.tar.gz` | Same two members as a tar.gz | Same as the zip |

## malware/

| File | What it is | Expected outcome |
|---|---|---|
| `malware/eicar.b64` | The EICAR antivirus test string, base64-encoded | `eicar_bytes()` returns the 68-byte string; a scanner reports it INFECTED |
| `malware/size_limits.json` | Upload limits used by size-boundary tests: 15 MB, 15 MB + 1 byte, 20 files | Values equal the limits in the upload design |

## MVP loader coverage (E0.8-T07)

Compared with TD §5.2. Every loader marked as MVP has at least one fixture, except one gap.

| MVP loader | Fixtures |
|---|---|
| `.md`, `.txt` | `sample.md`, `sample.txt` |
| `.eml` | `with_attachment.eml` |
| `.msg` | **none (gap)**: Outlook `.msg` is a binary format that is hard to synthesize; add one when the loader is built (E4.6) |
| `.json`, `.xml`, `.yaml`, OpenAPI, Swagger, FastMCP spec | `sample.json`, `sample.xml`, `sample.yaml`, `openapi.yaml`, `fastmcp_spec.json` (Swagger uses the same path as OpenAPI) |
| `.py`, `.sql`, `.js`, `.go`, `.cpp` | `sample.py`, `sample.sql`, `sample.js`, `sample.go`, `sample.cpp` |
| `.csv`, `.xlsx` | `sample.csv`, `multi_sheet.xlsx` |
| `.docx`, `.pdf` (text) | `sample.docx`, `text.pdf` |
| `.zip`, `.tar.gz` | `sample.zip`, `sample.tar.gz` |
| `.pdf` (scanned), `.png`, `.jpg`, `.jpeg`, `.tiff` | `scanned_full.pdf`, `scanned_mixed.pdf`, `scan.png`, `photo.jpg`, `scan.tiff` (`.jpeg` shares the JPEG path) |
